enableDatapointUpsertLogging.description: Optional. If true, logs to Cloud Logging errors relating to datapoint upserts. Under normal operation conditions, these log entries should be very rare. However, if incompatible datapoint updates are being uploaded to an index, a high volume of log entries may be generated in a short period of time. Note that logs may incur a cost, especially if the deployed index receives a high volume of datapoint upserts. Estimate your costs before enabling this option.

automaticResources.description: Optional. A description of resources that the DeployedIndex uses, which to large degree are decided by Vertex AI, and optionally allows only a modest additional configuration. If min_replica_count is not set, the default value is 2 (we don't provide SLA when min_replica_count=1). If max_replica_count is not set, the default value is min_replica_count. The max allowed replica count is 1000.

reservedIpRanges.description: Optional. A list of reserved ip ranges under the VPC network that can be used for this DeployedIndex. If set, we will deploy the index within the provided ip ranges. Otherwise, the index might be deployed to any ip ranges under the provided VPC network. The value should be the name of the address (https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/addresses) Example: ['vertex-ai-ip-range']. For more information about subnets and network IP ranges, please see https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/subnets#manually_created_subnet_ip_ranges.

indexSyncTime.description: Output only. The DeployedIndex may depend on various data on its original Index. Additionally when certain changes to the original Index are being done (e.g. when what the Index contains is being changed) the DeployedIndex may be asynchronously updated in the background to reflect these changes. If this timestamp's value is at least the Index.update_time of the original Index, it means that this DeployedIndex and the original Index are in sync. If this timestamp is older, then to see which updates this DeployedIndex already contains (and which it does not), one must list the operations that are running on the original Index. Only the successfully completed Operations with update_time equal or before this sync time are contained in this DeployedIndex.

enableAccessLogging.description: Optional. If true, private endpoint's access logs are sent to Cloud Logging. These logs are like standard server access logs, containing information like timestamp and latency for each MatchRequest. Note that logs may incur a cost, especially if the deployed index receives a high queries per second rate (QPS). Estimate your costs before enabling this option.

deploymentGroup.description: Optional. The deployment group can be no longer than 64 characters (eg: 'test', 'prod'). If not set, we will use the 'default' deployment group. Creating `deployment_groups` with `reserved_ip_ranges` is a recommended practice when the peered network has multiple peering ranges. This creates your deployments from predictable IP spaces for easier traffic administration. Also, one deployment_group (except 'default') can only be used with the same reserved_ip_ranges which means if the deployment_group has been used with reserved_ip_ranges: [a, b, c], using it with [a, b] or [d, e] is disallowed. Note: we only support up to 5 deployment groups(not including 'default').

id.description: Required. The user specified ID of the DeployedIndex. The ID can be up to 128 characters long and must start with a letter and only contain letters, numbers, and underscores. The ID must be unique within the project it is created in.

instanceType.description: The format of the instance that the Model accepts. Vertex AI will convert compatible batch prediction input instance formats to the specified format. Supported values are: * `object`: Each input is converted to JSON object format. * For `bigquery`, each row is converted to an object. * For `jsonl`, each line of the JSONL input must be an object. * Does not apply to `csv`, `file-list`, `tf-record`, or `tf-record-gzip`. * `array`: Each input is converted to JSON array format. * For `bigquery`, each row is converted to an array. The order of columns is determined by the BigQuery column order, unless included_fields is populated. included_fields must be populated for specifying field orders. * For `jsonl`, if each line of the JSONL input is an object, included_fields must be populated for specifying field orders. * Does not apply to `csv`, `file-list`, `tf-record`, or `tf-record-gzip`. If not specified, Vertex AI converts the batch prediction input as follows: * For `bigquery` and `csv`, the behavior is the same as `array`. The order of columns is the same as defined in the file or table, unless included_fields is populated. * For `jsonl`, the prediction instance format is determined by each line of the input. * For `tf-record`/`tf-record-gzip`, each record will be converted to an object in the format of `{"b64": }`, where `` is the Base64-encoded string of the content of the record. * For `file-list`, each file in the list will be converted to an object in the format of `{"b64": }`, where `` is the Base64-encoded string of the content of the file.

includedFields.description: Fields that will be included in the prediction instance that is sent to the Model. If instance_type is `array`, the order of field names in included_fields also determines the order of the values in the array. When included_fields is populated, excluded_fields must be empty. The input must be JSONL with objects at each line, BigQuery or TfRecord.

keyField.description: The name of the field that is considered as a key. The values identified by the key field is not included in the transformed instances that is sent to the Model. This is similar to specifying this name of the field in excluded_fields. In addition, the batch prediction output will not include the instances. Instead the output will only include the value of the key field, in a field named `key` in the output: * For `jsonl` output format, the output will have a `key` field instead of the `instance` field. * For `csv`/`bigquery` output format, the output will have have a `key` column instead of the instance feature columns. The input must be JSONL with objects at each line, CSV, BigQuery or TfRecord.

excludedFields.description: Fields that will be excluded in the prediction instance that is sent to the Model. Excluded will be attached to the batch prediction output if key_field is not specified. When excluded_fields is populated, included_fields must be empty. The input must be JSONL with objects at each line, BigQuery or TfRecord.

The supported optimization objectives: * "minimize-rmse" (default) - Minimize root-mean-squared error (RMSE). * "minimize-mae" - Minimize mean-absolute error (MAE). * "minimize-rmsle" - Minimize root-mean-squared log error (RMSLE). * "minimize-rmspe" - Minimize root-mean-squared percentage error (RMSPE). * "minimize-wape-mae" - Minimize the combination of weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) and mean-absolute-error (MAE). * "minimize-quantile-loss" - Minimize the quantile loss at the quantiles defined in `quantiles`. * "minimize-mape" - Minimize the mean absolute percentage error.

trainBudgetMilliNodeHours.description: Required. The train budget of creating this model, expressed in milli node hours i.e. 1,000 value in this field means 1 node hour. The training cost of the model will not exceed this budget. The final cost will be attempted to be close to the budget, though may end up being (even) noticeably smaller - at the backend's discretion. This especially may happen when further model training ceases to provide any improvements. If the budget is set to a value known to be insufficient to train a model for the given dataset, the training won't be attempted and will error. The train budget must be between 1,000 and 72,000 milli node hours, inclusive.

If the budget is set to a value known to be insufficient to train a model for the given dataset, the training won't be attempted and will error. The train budget must be between 1,000 and 72,000 milli node hours, inclusive.

On create an A1 (Personal) agent may omit it and the control plane defaults it to the caller; an A2 (CoWorker) agent must set it explicitly. `owner.id` must be an *obfuscated* Gaia id. A raw Gaia id is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the rule -- both forms are strings of decimal digits, so the surface would otherwise have two indistinguishable spellings of one identity. Not yet: `UpdateAgent` currently rejects a change to this field. The control plane authorizes every agent method against the owner Gaia id it persists internally at create time, and the update path does not maintain that copy — so a field write here would move the reported owner without moving the one access control uses. disableMemory.description: Optional. If true, memory is disabled for the agent as a whole: across every task it runs, the agent neither reads existing memories into the prompt nor forms new ones. Memory is on by default, and this is the setting that wins. A task may turn memory off for itself alone with `TaskSpec.scope.memory_config.disable_memory`, but cannot turn it back on while this is true; the two are OR'ed. This level wins because it is the mutable one. Turning it on has to cover the tasks that already exist, whose stored specs still say whatever they were created with, so the agent's current value is re-applied every time a session opens, including on a resume. Memories already stored are retained and stay readable by the agent's users; this governs only whether the agent can access and modify them.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1AgentMemoryC.description: Agent-level memory settings. These apply across every task the agent runs and every user of the agent: this is an agent-wide control, not a per-user one. To turn memory off for a single end user of a shared agent, the calling surface sets `TaskSpec.scope.memory_config.disable_memory` on that user's tasks.

This column must be available at forecast.

availableAtForecastColumns.description: Names of columns that are available and provided when a forecast is requested. These columns contain information for the given entity (identified by the time_series_identifier_column column) that is known at forecast. For example, predicted weather for a specific day.

optimizationObjective.description: Objective function the model is optimizing towards. The training process creates a model that optimizes the value of the objective function over the validation set. The supported optimization objectives: * "minimize-rmse" (default) - Minimize root-mean-squared error (RMSE). * "minimize-mae" - Minimize mean-absolute error (MAE). * "minimize-rmsle" - Minimize root-mean-squared log error (RMSLE). * "minimize-rmspe" - Minimize root-mean-squared percentage error (RMSPE). * "minimize-wape-mae" - Minimize the combination of weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) and mean-absolute-error (MAE). * "minimize-quantile-loss" - Minimize the quantile loss at the quantiles defined in `quantiles`. * "minimize-mape" - Minimize the mean absolute percentage error.

trainBudgetMilliNodeHours.description: Required. The train budget of creating this model, expressed in milli node hours i.e. 1,000 value in this field means 1 node hour. The training cost of the model will not exceed this budget. The final cost will be attempted to be close to the budget, though may end up being (even) noticeably smaller - at the backend's discretion. This especially may happen when further model training ceases to provide any improvements. If the budget is set to a value known to be insufficient to train a model for the given dataset, the training won't be attempted and will error. The train budget must be between 1,000 and 72,000 milli node hours, inclusive.

minNumSteps.description: Minimum number of steps for a trial to complete. Trials which do not have a measurement with num_steps > min_num_steps won't be considered for early stopping. It's ok to set it to 0, and a trial can be early stopped at any stage. By default, min_num_steps is set to be one-tenth of the max_num_steps. When use_steps is false, this field is set to the minimum elapsed seconds.

autoregressiveOrder.description: The number of Trial measurements used in autoregressive model for value prediction. A trial won't be considered early stopping if has fewer measurement points.

maxNumSteps.description: Steps used in predicting the final objective for early stopped trials. In general, it's set to be the same as the defined steps in training / tuning. When use_steps is false, this field is set to the maximum elapsed seconds.

learningRateParameterName.description: The hyper-parameter name used in the tuning job that stands for learning rate. Leave it blank if learning rate is not in a parameter in tuning. The learning_rate is used to estimate the objective value of the ongoing trial.

useSeconds.description: This bool determines whether or not the rule is applied based on elapsed_secs or steps. If use_seconds==false, the early stopping decision is made according to the predicted objective values according to the target steps. If use_seconds==true, elapsed_secs is used instead of steps. Also, in this case, the parameters max_num_steps and min_num_steps are overloaded to contain max_elapsed_seconds and min_elapsed_seconds.

A value the resolved model does not accept leaves its own default standing.

model.description: Optional. Publisher model resource name (an `aiplatform.googleapis.com/PublisherModel`) of the form "publishers/{publisher}/models/{model}", e.g. "publishers/anthropic/models/claude-opus-4-8" or "publishers/google/models/gemini-3-flash". The project-qualified form "projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/{publisher}/models/{model}" is also accepted. When it is used, the project and location it carries take precedence over both dynamic project/location resolution and the actor config defaults. Model selection cannot be updated after task creation right now though it might be supported in the future. Empty means the actor's default gemini model.

maxOutputTokens.description: Optional. Maximum number of tokens the model may generate in each call, including any thinking tokens it spends before answering. Must not be negative; zero leaves the backend default standing. The cap also applies to the calls that summarize the task's history when its context is compacted, so a model that thinks at a high effort level may need a larger value to return a summary at all.

parameters.description: If/when a Trial is generated or selected from this Context, its Parameters will match any parameters specified here. (I.e. if this context specifies parameter name:'a' int_value:3, then a resulting Trial will have int_value:3 for its parameter named 'a'.) Note that we first attempt to match existing REQUESTED Trials with contexts, and if there are no matches, we generate suggestions in the subspace defined by the parameters specified here. NOTE: a Context without any Parameters matches the entire feasible search space.

If true, Runtime owner is using EUC and does not require the above permission as VM no longer use default Compute Engine SA, but a P4SA.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1LogprobsResu.description: The log probabilities of the tokens generated by the model. This is useful for understanding the model's confidence in its predictions and for debugging. For example, you can use log probabilities to identify when the model is making a less confident prediction or to explore alternative responses that the model considered. A low log probability can also indicate that the model is "hallucinating" or generating factually incorrect information.

confidenceScores.description: The confidence scores for the support references. This list is parallel to the `grounding_chunk_indices` list. A score is a value between 0.0 and 1.0, with a higher score indicating a higher confidence that the reference supports the claim. For Gemini 2.0 and before, this list has the same size as `grounding_chunk_indices`. For Gemini 2.5 and later, this list is empty and should be ignored.

groundingChunkIndices.description: A list of indices into the `grounding_chunks` field of the `GroundingMetadata` message. These indices specify which grounding chunks support the claim made in the content segment. For example, if this field has the values `[1, 3]`, it means that `grounding_chunks[1]` and `grounding_chunks[3]` are the sources for the claim in the content segment.

renderedParts.description: Indices into the `rendered_parts` field of the `GroundingMetadata` message. These indices specify which rendered parts are associated with this support message.

segment.description: The content segment that this support message applies to.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1GroundingSup.description: A collection of supporting references for a segment or part of the model's response.

To explicitly set a timezone to the cron tab, apply a prefix in the cron tab: "CRON_TZ=${IANA_TIME_ZONE}" or "TZ=${IANA_TIME_ZONE}". The ${IANA_TIME_ZONE} may only be a valid string from IANA time zone database. For example, "CRON_TZ=America/New_York 1 * * * *", or "TZ=America/New_York 1 * * * *".

As a tradeoff, it requires longer indexing time and manual triggering of index rebuild via the ImportRagFiles and UpdateRagCorpus API.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1Probe.description: Probe describes a health check to be performed against a container to determine whether it is alive or ready to receive traffic.

timeoutSeconds.description: Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Must be greater or equal to period_seconds. Maps to Kubernetes probe argument 'timeoutSeconds'.

successThreshold.description: Number of consecutive successes before the probe is considered successful. Defaults to 1. Minimum value is 1. Maps to Kubernetes probe argument 'successThreshold'.

httpGet.description: HttpGetAction probes the health of a container by sending an HTTP GET request.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Number of seconds to wait before starting the probe. Defaults to 0. Minimum value is 0. Maps to Kubernetes probe argument 'initialDelaySeconds'.

exec.description: ExecAction probes the health of a container by executing a command.

failureThreshold.description: Number of consecutive failures before the probe is considered failed. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1. Maps to Kubernetes probe argument 'failureThreshold'.

grpc.description: GrpcAction probes the health of a container by sending a gRPC request.

periodSeconds.description: How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Default to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Must be less than timeout_seconds. Maps to Kubernetes probe argument 'periodSeconds'.

tcpSocket.description: TcpSocketAction probes the health of a container by opening a TCP socket connection.

expression.description: Required. The cron expression, e.g. "0 8 * * MON-FRI". Any field may also be `?` or `?/step` to let the service pick the value, so that schedules do not all fire at the same moment: `?` picks one value in the field's range, and `?/step` picks a start within the first step and repeats every step from there. The pick is made once, when the schedule is created or updated, and the expression is stored with the picked values in place of `?` (e.g. "?/30 * * * *" is stored as "17-59/30 * * * *"); sending a `?` again picks new values.

timeZone.description: Optional. Optional IANA time zone name, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". Defaults to UTC.

endOffset.description: End offset in time of the word relative to the start of the audio. Present when timestamp_granularities contains "word".

speaker.description: Optional. Speaker label for this word (e.g. "spk_1", "spk_2"). Present when diarization_mode is set in TranscriptionConfig.

GoogleTypeInterval.description: Represents a time interval, encoded as a Timestamp start (inclusive) and a Timestamp end (exclusive). The start must be less than or equal to the end. When the start equals the end, the interval is empty (matches no time). When both start and end are unspecified, the interval matches any time.

startTime.description: Optional. Inclusive start of the interval. If specified, a Timestamp matching this interval will have to be the same or after the start.

endTime.description: Optional. Exclusive end of the interval. If specified, a Timestamp matching this interval will have to be before the end.

minValue.description: The minimum permissible value for this feature.

maxValue.description: The maximum permissible value for this feature.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1ExplanationM.description: Domain details of the input feature value. Provides numeric information about the feature, such as its range (min, max). If the feature has been pre-processed, for example with z-scoring, then it provides information about how to recover the original feature. For example, if the input feature is an image and it has been pre-processed to obtain 0-mean and stddev = 1 values, then original_mean, and original_stddev refer to the mean and stddev of the original feature (e.g. image tensor) from which input feature (with mean = 0 and stddev = 1) was obtained.

When this flag is set, the service may route traffic to other regions if a model is unavailable in the current region (e.g., to a `global` endpoint). If a fully-qualified model endpoint resource name with a different region than the request location is provided elsewhere in the request, this flag must be set to true or the request will fail.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1FeatureStats.description: Stats and Anomaly generated at specific timestamp for specific Feature. The start_time and end_time are used to define the time range of the dataset that current stats belongs to, e.g. prediction traffic is bucketed into prediction datasets by time window. If the Dataset is not defined by time window, start_time = end_time. Timestamp of the stats and anomalies always refers to end_time. Raw stats and anomalies are stored in stats_uri or anomaly_uri in the tensorflow defined protos. Field data_stats contains almost identical information with the raw stats in Vertex AI defined proto, for UI to display.

endTime.description: The end timestamp of window where stats were generated. For objectives where time window doesn't make sense (e.g. Featurestore Snapshot Monitoring), end_time indicates the timestamp of the data used to generate stats (e.g. timestamp we take snapshots for feature values).

statsUri.description: Path of the stats file for current feature values in Cloud Storage bucket. Format: gs:////stats. Example: gs://monitoring_bucket/feature_name/stats. Stats are stored as binary format with Protobuf message [tensorflow.metadata.v0.FeatureNameStatistics](https://github.com/tensorflow/metadata/blob/master/tensorflow_metadata/proto/v0/statistics.proto).

score.description: Feature importance score, only populated when cross-feature monitoring is enabled. updateMask.description: Optional. The list of fields of `cache_config` to update. Supported paths are `disable_cache`, `retention_config` (and its subfields such as `retention_config.retention_type`), and the special value `*`; any other path returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Fields not covered by the mask keep their stored value. If the mask is omitted, it is treated as an implied mask covering the fields populated in `cache_config`, so updating one field never clears another. `retention_config` is covered only when the request carries it. `disable_cache` is always covered: it is a bare `bool`, so the server cannot tell a request that omits it from one that sets it to `false`. `*` requests full replacement of the resource: every settable field is written from the request, clearing `retention_config` when the request omits it. It cannot be combined with other paths. Prefer naming fields explicitly -- a caller that sends `*` without knowing about a field added to `CacheConfig` later would silently reset that field.

testIamPermissions.description: Returns permissions that a caller has on the specified resource. If the resource does not exist, this will return an empty set of permissions, not a `NOT_FOUND` error. Note: This operation is designed to be used for building permission-aware UIs and command-line tools, not for authorization checking. This operation may "fail open" without warning.

list.description: Lists the agents in a location that belong to the caller. An agent belongs to the end user recorded as its owner when it was created, so the response holds that caller's agents and no others. It is empty for a caller that is not an end user, and an agent with no recorded owner is listed for nobody.

parent.description: Required. The resource name of the location to list agents from. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`.

orderBy.description: Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. Supported fields: * `created` * `updated` Use `desc` after a field name for descending order. Example: `created desc`.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of agents to return. The service may return fewer than this value. The maximum page size is 100; values above 100 will be coerced to 100. If unspecified, the default page size is 10.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous AgentService.ListAgents call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.

filter.description: Optional. An [AIP-160](https://google.aip.dev/160) filter over the returned agents. An empty filter returns the unfiltered collection. Supported fields, and the operators each accepts: * `created` * `updated` * `base_agent` * `metadata.agent_type` `created` and `updated` are timestamps and take an RFC-3339 value, for example `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z`. Supported operators: `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `:`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (equivalently `-`), and parentheses. Note that `OR` binds more tightly than `AND`, so `a AND b OR c` means `a AND (b OR c)`; parentheses are recommended, not required. `metadata.agent_type` accepts only the value `"default_agent"`, matched exactly: `metadata.agent_type:"default_agent"` selects the caller's default agent, of which there is at most one, and the negated form selects the rest. Any other value is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` rather than an empty page -- `metadata` is an opaque blob, so only this one marker is indexed, and the server cannot answer a question about the others. An agent designated before the server began recording the marker is not matched by the positive form; there is no backfill. `base_agent` accepts `=` and `!=` against the value an agent was created with, and selects only among the agents you own: an agent that belongs to the project rather than to a user is never returned by a filter naming it, including the negated form. An agent created before the server began recording the value is not matched either. Example: `created > "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" AND updated < "2026-08-09T00:00:00Z"`. IMPORTANT -- `base_agent` and `metadata.agent_type` select only among the agents you own. An agent that belongs to the project rather than to a user is never returned by a filter naming either of them, including a negated one: `base_agent != "some-value"` returns your matching agents and no project-owned agents at all. Filtering on `created` or `updated` alone is unaffected and still spans both. If you want every agent in the project, do not filter on these two fields. Not supported: any field other than those listed above, wildcards other than `field:*`, bare literals with no field name, functions, and the regular-expression operators `=~` and `!~`. A filter that names an unsupported field, exceeds 1000 characters, or nests parentheses more than 5 deep fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

delete.description: Deletes an agent.

name.description: Required. The resource name of the agent to delete. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}`.

force.description: Optional. If true, any `Task` belonging to this agent is deleted along with it. If false or unset and the agent still has at least one `Task`, the request fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` and nothing is deleted. This governs `Task` and nothing else. Resources the agent owns but a caller never named -- its AI Application and the tenant project bound to it, its Workspace identity, its service-extension binding -- are torn down with the agent on every delete, whatever this field says.

name.description: Identifier. The resource name of the agent. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}`.

updateMask.description: Optional. The list of fields to update. If not present, all fields are updated.

resource.description: REQUIRED: The resource for which the policy is being specified. See [Resource names](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/resource_names) for the appropriate value for this field.

setIamPolicy.description: Sets the access control policy on the specified resource. Replaces any existing policy. Can return `NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and `PERMISSION_DENIED` errors.

name.description: Required. The resource name of the agent to retrieve. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}`.

get.description: Retrieves an agent.

getIamPolicy.description: Gets the access control policy for a resource. Returns an empty policy if the resource exists and does not have a policy set.

resource.description: REQUIRED: The resource for which the policy is being requested. See [Resource names](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/resource_names) for the appropriate value for this field.

options.requestedPolicyVersion.description: Optional. The maximum policy version that will be used to format the policy. Valid values are 0, 1, and 3. Requests specifying an invalid value will be rejected. Requests for policies with any conditional role bindings must specify version 3. Policies with no conditional role bindings may specify any valid value or leave the field unset. The policy in the response might use the policy version that you specified, or it might use a lower policy version. For example, if you specify version 3, but the policy has no conditional role bindings, the response uses version 1. To learn which resources support conditions in their IAM policies, see the [IAM documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/help/conditions/resource-policies).

parent.description: Required. The resource name of the location to create the agent in. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`.

name.description: The name of the operation resource to be deleted.

delete.description: Deletes a long-running operation. This method indicates that the client is no longer interested in the operation result. It does not cancel the operation. If the server doesn't support this method, it returns `google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`.

name.description: The name of the operation resource to be cancelled.

cancel.description: Starts asynchronous cancellation on a long-running operation. The server makes a best effort to cancel the operation, but success is not guaranteed. If the server doesn't support this method, it returns `google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`. Clients can use Operations.GetOperation or other methods to check whether the cancellation succeeded or whether the operation completed despite cancellation. On successful cancellation, the operation is not deleted; instead, it becomes an operation with an Operation.error value with a google.rpc.Status.code of `1`, corresponding to `Code.CANCELLED`.

name.description: The name of the operation resource.

get.description: Gets the latest state of a long-running operation. Clients can use this method to poll the operation result at intervals as recommended by the API service.

returnPartialSuccess.description: When set to `true`, operations that are reachable are returned as normal, and those that are unreachable are returned in the ListOperationsResponse.unreachable field. This can only be `true` when reading across collections. For example, when `parent` is set to `"projects/example/locations/-"`. This field is not supported by default and will result in an `UNIMPLEMENTED` error if set unless explicitly documented otherwise in service or product specific documentation.

name.description: The name of the operation's parent resource.

list.description: Lists operations that match the specified filter in the request. If the server doesn't support this method, it returns `UNIMPLEMENTED`.

wait.description: Waits until the specified long-running operation is done or reaches at most a specified timeout, returning the latest state. If the operation is already done, the latest state is immediately returned. If the timeout specified is greater than the default HTTP/RPC timeout, the HTTP/RPC timeout is used. If the server does not support this method, it returns `google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`. Note that this method is on a best-effort basis. It may return the latest state before the specified timeout (including immediately), meaning even an immediate response is no guarantee that the operation is done.

name.description: The name of the operation resource to wait on.

timeout.description: The maximum duration to wait before timing out. If left blank, the wait will be at most the time permitted by the underlying HTTP/RPC protocol. If RPC context deadline is also specified, the shorter one will be used.

recursive.description: Optional. If `true`, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace to list. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous ListWorkspaceArtifacts call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other fields of the request except `page_size` must match the call that provided the page token. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer than this value, including none on a page that is not the last. If unspecified or 0, at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000. A negative value is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. `/workspace/userdata`. Must be `/workspace` or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Defaults to `/workspace`.

filter.description: Optional. An AIP-160 filter expression that entries must match, e.g. `type = FILE AND mime_type = "image/*"`. Empty matches every entry. Supported fields: * `type` -- `FILE` or `DIRECTORY` (see `TaskArtifactFile.Type`), case-sensitive. * `mime_type` -- a media type in double quotes, e.g. `"text/csv"`. `*` is a wildcard, so `"image/*"` matches every image type. Directories have an empty `mime_type`. Comparisons use `=` or `!=` and combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (or `-`) and parentheses. A filter that is not valid AIP-160, or that uses another field or operator, is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The filter selects which entries are returned, not which directories are walked: with `recursive`, `type = FILE` still returns the files in subdirectories.

list.description: Lists the files and directories in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries that match `filter` are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

add.description: Adds a file, folder or site stored in Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint or another third-party store as an artifact. The service persists `link_json_metadata` to Cloud Storage as a JSON metadata reference (a `.link.json` file), and links it to a parent resource: a task, named by `task`, or a collaborative project, named by `collaborative_project`. This method is idempotent with respect to the linked entity, identified by `link_json_metadata.provider` and `link_json_metadata.source_artifact_id`, or `link_json_metadata.uri` when `source_artifact_id` is unset: adding an entity that the parent already has does not add another artifact, and returns the same `artifact_id`.

task.description: Optional. The task to link the file to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} Exactly one of `task` and `collaborative_project` must be set.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.pptx`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.pptx`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace holds the file. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type to convert the file to: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid.

preview.description: Returns a file converted for a preview, such as a PDF of a .pptx. A server-streaming RPC. The response body is the converted file's bytes, with its media type as the `Content-Type`. The server converts the file as it is stored now, on every call, and stores nothing. A PDF asked for as a PDF is returned as stored. Fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when the file cannot be converted (an unsupported format, too large, or unreadable), with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when the conversion takes too long, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when conversion is busy or not available; the last two may succeed on a retry.

remove.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file in the task's workspace, under `/workspace/`, e.g. `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`. A path outside `/workspace/`, including a relative path, or a path with a `..` segment fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A directory path, or a task in a terminal state, fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is `true`, in which case the call succeeds and changes nothing.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace holds the file. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

downloadArtifact.description: Downloads a file from a task's workspace as a stream of chunks. A server-streaming RPC. The response body is the file's raw bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type`. At most 1 GiB. Like ListTaskArtifacts, reads from the running sandbox when there is one, so a file the agent has just written is returned even before it reaches storage.

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type to return: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. a .docx or .pptx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of the file to read, e.g. "/workspace/report.md". Must be under "/workspace", at most 1024 characters, and not contain a ".." segment.

task.description: Required. The task to download from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

create.description: Creates a task without opening a live channel. Convenient for scheduled/background tasks where the caller does not need to drive the execution interactively; observe progress later via StreamTask (or by reconnecting to CreateTaskBidiStream with a `subscribe_task` request).

userContext.timeZone.description: Optional. The user's IANA time zone name, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". The agent uses it to interpret and present dates and times, e.g. to resolve "tomorrow morning".

parent.description: Required. The parent agent that owns this task. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}

uniqueCreationToken.description: Optional. Optional idempotency token to guarantee the task is created only once. Suggest a UUID. A create carrying a token that a live task of the same agent already holds fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`, naming that task in the response. The token is free again once that task finishes.

userContext.location.description: Optional. The user's coarse, human-readable location, e.g. "Mountain View, CA, US". Must be no more precise than city level; never send street addresses, postal codes, or coordinates. The agent uses it for location-dependent requests, e.g. weather or nearby places.

userContext.channel.description: Optional. How the user's input reached the agent. Leave unset when the user talks to the agent directly in an AI-native interface.
enumDescriptions: Default. The user is talking to the agent directly in an AI-native interface (e.g. the Gemini Enterprise app, Workspace Studio, or the Gemini app), or the channel is unknown. The agent applies no channel-specific behavior.

A threaded conversation on a communication product where the agent is one participant, e.g. a Google Chat DM or space, or a comment thread on a document. The agent keeps its reply short and conversational, suited to a thread that others can read, and may ask a follow-up question.
An email message. The agent writes a complete, self-contained reply suited to email, and avoids follow-up questions it could anticipate, since each round trip is slow.

name.description: Required. The task or collaborative project to upload to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

upload.description: Uploads a file. The file is sent as media: post it to this method's URL with an `/upload` prefix, e.g. `/upload/v1beta1/{name}:upload`, carrying `path` as request metadata and the file's bytes as the media content. The task must not be in a terminal state, and an existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 10 GiB.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to retrieve. Both name forms are accepted: * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/tasks/{task}

get.description: Gets a task.

cancel.description: Deprecated: use `CancelTaskLro` instead. This method keeps the same cancellation semantics but returns `Task` directly, which forecloses the future cascade behaviour on recurring parents that only an `Operation` return type can express. Cancels a task, out-of-band by id. Drains any in-progress work and moves the task to CANCELLED. Use this when there is no active stream (e.g. a scheduled or background task) or when a caller other than the streaming client cancels. A task may also be cancelled in-band via the bidi cancel_task end_request; the two paths are equivalent. Cancellation semantics: * Idempotent: cancelling an already-terminal task is a no-op that returns the current Task; concurrent/duplicate cancels collapse to one CANCELLED. * First terminal state wins: once the task is CANCELLED/COMPLETED/FAILED, later cancels have no effect. * Cancel takes precedence over complete_task: a cancel arriving while (or after) a client half-closes with complete_task still drives the task to CANCELLED rather than letting it finish.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to cancel. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

nextStepSeqNum.description: Optional. The next step sequence number to resume from. When zero, streams from the beginning of the available trajectory.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to stream. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

continuationToken.description: Optional. Opaque resume cursor, as issued on TaskServerEvent.continuation_token. Replay continues immediately after the event that carried the token. Takes precedence over next_step_seq_num when both are set. A token this stream cannot redeem is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than silently falling back to the numeric cursor, so a client cannot mistake a rejected resume for a replay from the start; reconnect without a token instead. That covers a malformed token, one issued by a connection whose delta streaming differs from this one's (see TaskSpec.delta_streaming), one issued while the server derived task status differently, and any token on a recurring task. A token names a position in the task it was issued on; send it only to that task. It carries no task id, so a token from another task is not rejected, and what it returns is undefined. A token whose position is past the events stored so far is not an error either, because storage can trail the live stream that issued the token: the replay skips everything up to that position, so a snapshot may return no events.

snapshot.description: Optional. If true, streams only the events produced up to the current point in time and terminates the stream once all existing events are sent, rather than tailing and waiting for future events.

stream.description: Read-only server-stream of a task's execution by id: trajectory steps and status changes, resumable from a step sequence number. Unlike CreateTaskBidiStream, it does not accept client inputs -- use it to observe or replay a task (the trajectory is not stored on the Task resource). This is the entry point for *observers*: it tails the trajectory from interaction storage without restoring the runtime actor, so it adds no restore latency and continues to follow output that a participant driving the task on a CreateTaskBidiStream connection produces. Observe-only clients should prefer this over a subscribe_task connect on CreateTaskBidiStream, which restores the actor and is meant for clients that will send input.

suspend.description: Suspends a task, pausing its active turn or scheduling loop and transitioning the status to SUSPENDED. The underlying runtime session remains resumable.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to suspend. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

parent.description: Required. The parent to list tasks under. Both forms are accepted and scope the listing differently: * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent} -- tasks assigned to that agent. * projects/{project}/locations/{location} -- all tasks in the location.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of tasks to return. The service may return fewer. If unspecified (or <= 0), at most 50 are returned. The maximum is 100; larger values are capped to 100.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token from a previous ListTasks call.

orderBy.description: Optional. Sort order, e.g. "create_time desc". The sortable fields are `create_time` and `update_time`. Defaults to "create_time desc".

filter.description: Optional. A filter expression, e.g. "status=WORKING". Lineage filters pick how much of a task tree to fetch: * "parent_task_id=" -- direct children only (progressive disclosure, one level per call). * "root_task_id=" -- the whole tree in one flat collection. Label filters support filtering by task labels: * "labels.=" -- match tasks with the given label key and value. Multiple label filters can be combined with AND. Multiple values for the same key can be combined with OR, e.g., "labels.foo=bar OR labels.foo=baz". Status filters restrict the listing to tasks in the given statuses: * "status=" -- e.g. "status=WORKING". Multiple statuses can be combined with OR, e.g., "status=WORKING OR status=IDLE". Both page normally via `page_size`/`page_token`, and both are ordered by `order_by` (default "create_time desc"), not by tree shape. A whole-tree page is therefore not a subtree: a child can arrive before its parent, so the client buffers by `parent_task_id` and renders as parents resolve.

list.description: Lists tasks under a parent. Supports filtering (e.g. by status or assigned_agent) so a surface can show "my tasks".

deleteArtifact.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file under `/workspace/userdata/` (for example, `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`). Paths outside `/workspace/userdata/`, `/workspace/userdata` itself, relative paths, or paths with `.` or `..` segments fail with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Directory paths and tasks in a terminal state fail with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is true, in which case the call succeeds with an empty response.

task.description: Required. The task to delete from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

patch.description: Updates a task's mutable fields (e.g. schedule, priority, title). Typically allowed while the task is IDLE.

name.description: Identifier. Resource name of the task.

updateMask.description: Required. The list of fields to update.

listArtifacts.description: Lists the files in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token from a previous ListTaskArtifacts call. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. "/workspace/userdata". Must be "/workspace" or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a ".." segment. Defaults to "/workspace".

recursive.description: Optional. If true, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer. If unspecified (or <= 0), at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; larger values are capped to 1000.

task.description: Required. The task whose workspace to list. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

name.description: Required. The name of the task to resume. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

resume.description: Resumes a suspended task, transitioning it back to an active state (WORKING or QUEUED).

name.description: Required. The name of the task to delete. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

operateOnSelf.description: Optional. Whether to skip cascading deletion to all descendant subtasks. Defaults to false (cascades to all descendants by default). Matches google.cloud.aiplatform.master.CancelTaskRequest.operate_on_self. Behavior: UNSET or false ⇒ cascade: delete this task and every non-terminal descendant (gated by Mendel flag sobi_enable_cascading_delete_task; returns FAILED_PRECONDITION when the flag is OFF and the task has non-terminal children). true ⇒ delete this task only. Each descendant deletion signals the runtime for the live-session case (Actor.OnCancel finalizes trajectory + reclaims sandbox VM) before removing the Sobi DB rows, matching the single-DeleteTask contract.

delete.description: Deletes a task. Long-running because deletion cascades: it cancels any active run (WORKING / REQUIRES_ACTION / SUSPENDED tasks are cancelled-then-deleted, not rejected), and cleans up the task's bound resources -- environment, generated artifacts, and the runtime trajectory/sessions. The operation completes when the cascade finishes; on success the response is google.protobuf.Empty.

path.description: Required. Absolute destination path, e.g. "/workspace/userdata/input.csv". Must be under "/workspace/userdata/" and at most 1024 characters; relative paths and paths containing a ".." segment are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

task.description: Required. The task to upload into. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

uploadArtifact.description: Uploads a file into a task's workspace. A client-streaming RPC: the request body is the file's raw bytes, relayed to storage a chunk at a time, so neither ESF nor this server holds the whole file. A broken connection restarts the upload from zero. `path` must be an absolute path under `/workspace/userdata/`. The task must not be in a terminal state. An existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 1 GiB.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.md`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.md`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

name.description: Required. The task or collaborative project to download from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type of the rendition: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

download.description: Downloads a file. The response body is the file's bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` that names the file. Media is the default and only representation, so no `alt` parameter is needed. A preview sets `processing_config` and gets a rendition of the file in place of the file, such as a PDF of a .pptx: the response body is the rendition, with its own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` name that ends in its extension. Without `processing_config` the response is always the stored file.

parent.description: Required. The location to retrieve the Skills in. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`

query.description: Optional. The query to find matching skills.

topK.description: Optional. The maximum number of skills to return. The service may return fewer than this value. If unspecified, at most 10 skills will be returned. The maximum value is 100.

get.description: Get a Skill.

name.description: Required. The resource name of the Skill to retrieve. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/skills/{skill}`

parent.description: Required. The location to create the Skill in. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`

skillId.description: Required. The ID to use for the Skill, which will become the final component of the Skill's resource name. If not provided, a system-generated ID will be used. The media type to convert the file to: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid.

preview.description: Returns a file converted for a preview, such as a PDF of a .pptx. A server-streaming RPC. The response body is the converted file's bytes, with its media type as the `Content-Type`. The server converts the file as it is stored now, on every call, and stores nothing. A PDF asked for as a PDF is returned as stored. Fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when the file cannot be converted (an unsupported format, too large, or unreadable), with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when the conversion takes too long, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when conversion is busy or not available; the last two may succeed on a retry.

list.description: Lists the files and directories in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries that match `filter` are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

recursive.description: Optional. If `true`, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

filter.description: Optional. An AIP-160 filter expression that entries must match, e.g. `type = FILE AND mime_type = "image/*"`. Empty matches every entry. Supported fields: * `type` -- `FILE` or `DIRECTORY` (see `TaskArtifactFile.Type`), case-sensitive. * `mime_type` -- a media type in double quotes, e.g. `"text/csv"`. `*` is a wildcard, so `"image/*"` matches every image type. Directories have an empty `mime_type`. Comparisons use `=` or `!=` and combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (or `-`) and parentheses. A filter that is not valid AIP-160, or that uses another field or operator, is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The filter selects which entries are returned, not which directories are walked: with `recursive`, `type = FILE` still returns the files in subdirectories.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer than this value, including none on a page that is not the last. If unspecified or 0, at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000. A negative value is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous ListWorkspaceArtifacts call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other fields of the request except `page_size` must match the call that provided the page token. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. `/workspace/userdata`. Must be `/workspace` or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Defaults to `/workspace`.

remove.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file in the task's workspace, under `/workspace/`, e.g. `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`. A path outside `/workspace/`, including a relative path, or a path with a `..` segment fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A directory path, or a task in a terminal state, fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is `true`, in which case the call succeeds and changes nothing.

add.description: Adds a file, folder or site stored in Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint or another third-party store as an artifact. The service persists `link_json_metadata` to Cloud Storage as a JSON metadata reference (a `.link.json` file), and links it to a parent resource: a task, named by `task`, or a collaborative project, named by `collaborative_project`. This method is idempotent with respect to the linked entity, identified by `link_json_metadata.provider` and `link_json_metadata.source_artifact_id`, or `link_json_metadata.uri` when `source_artifact_id` is unset: adding an entity that the parent already has does not add another artifact, and returns the same `artifact_id`.

query.description: Query string that is a conjunction of field-restricted queries and/or field-restricted filters. Field-restricted queries and filters can be combined using `AND` to form a conjunction. A field query is in the form FIELD:QUERY. This implicitly checks if QUERY exists as a substring within Feature's FIELD. The QUERY and the FIELD are converted to a sequence of words (i.e. tokens) for comparison. This is done by: * Removing leading/trailing whitespace and tokenizing the search value. Characters that are not one of alphanumeric `[a-zA-Z0-9]`, underscore `_`, or asterisk `*` are treated as delimiters for tokens. `*` is treated as a wildcard that matches characters within a token. * Ignoring case. * Prepending an asterisk to the first and appending an asterisk to the last token in QUERY. A QUERY must be either a singular token or a phrase. A phrase is one or multiple words enclosed in double quotation marks ("). With phrases, the order of the words is important. Words in the phrase must be matching in order and consecutively. Supported FIELDs for field-restricted queries: * `feature_id` * `description` * `entity_type_id` Examples: * `feature_id: foo` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo` (eg. `foo`, `foofeature`, `barfoo`). * `feature_id: foo*feature` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo*feature` (eg. `foobarfeature`). * `feature_id: foo AND description: bar` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo` and description containing the substring `bar`. filter.description: Optional. Filter expression restricting which AnalyzedSessions are returned. Supports a subset of AIP-160: a closed `detection_time` window (both bounds required), an equality on `severity`, an equality on `agent_type`, and an equality on `session_id`, joined by `AND`. Each clause is optional, may appear at most once, and may appear in any order. The `severity` value is the **canonical** `Severity` enum name -- `SEVERITY_CRITICAL`, `SEVERITY_HIGH`, `SEVERITY_MEDIUM` or `SEVERITY_LOW`. Short forms such as `"CRITICAL"` are rejected, as is `SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED`. It matches sessions whose *maximum* severity equals that bucket: a session that fires at both LOW and CRITICAL matches `severity = "SEVERITY_CRITICAL"`, not `severity = "SEVERITY_LOW"`. The `agent_type` value is the canonical `AgentResource.AgentType` enum name -- `REASONING_ENGINE`, `CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE`, `GKE_WORKLOAD`, `GCE_INSTANCE`, `AGENT_TYPE_OTHER` or `AGENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` -- and matches sessions run by an agent on that runtime. Unlike `severity`, `agent_type` accepts its `UNSPECIFIED` value. The two are not analogous: a session always has a computed severity bucket, so `SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED` is never returned and filtering on it could only match nothing. `AGENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` *is* returned -- it is what `AnalyzedSession.agent_type` reports for an agent whose runtime was never recorded -- so it must remain filterable. The `session_id` value is a case-sensitive exact match (no substring or prefix matching) on `AnalyzedSession.session_id`. Unlike `severity` and `agent_type` it is not a closed enum, so any non-empty value is accepted; an empty value (`session_id = ""`) is rejected rather than treated as "no filter". Example (time window, severity and runtime): ``` detection_time >= "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" AND detection_time <= "2024-01-08T00:00:00Z" AND severity = "SEVERITY_CRITICAL" AND agent_type = "CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE" ``` If empty, results are restricted to the last 7 days with no severity, runtime, or session restriction. Other fields, additional operators, set membership (`IN`), and boolean combinations (`OR`, `NOT`, parentheses) are not yet supported.

orderBy.description: Optional. Comma-separated list of fields to sort by, following AIP-132 syntax. The default sort direction is ascending; append " desc" to a field to sort descending. Supported fields (any other field yields INVALID_ARGUMENT): * `latest_detection_time` - the session's most-recent flagged detection time. `latest_detection_time desc` puts the newest sessions first. * `max_severity_rank` - the session's bucketed maximum severity, ranked LOW=1 < MEDIUM=2 < HIGH=3 < CRITICAL=4. `max_severity_rank desc` puts the most-severe sessions first. * `agent_display_name` - the MonitoredAgent's display name. Sorted as a STRING (case-sensitive, code-point order). If empty, defaults to `latest_detection_time desc`. Multi-field sort (for example, `max_severity_rank desc, latest_detection_time desc`) is supported. The `order_by` value MUST match the value used on the call that minted any supplied `page_token` (AIP-158). Mismatches yield INVALID_ARGUMENT.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.md`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.md`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type of the rendition: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

name.description: Required. The task or collaborative project to download from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

download.description: Downloads a file. The response body is the file's bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` that names the file. Media is the default and only representation, so no `alt` parameter is needed. A preview sets `processing_config` and gets a rendition of the file in place of the file, such as a PDF of a .pptx: the response body is the rendition, with its own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` name that ends in its extension. Without `processing_config` the response is always the stored file.

parent.description: Required. The resource name of the Location to list the BatchPredictionJobs from. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`

pageToken.description: The standard list page token. Typically obtained via ListBatchPredictionJobsResponse.next_page_token of the previous JobService.ListBatchPredictionJobs call.

readMask.description: Mask specifying which fields to read.

filter.description: The standard list filter. Supported fields: * `display_name` supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. * `model_display_name` supports `=`, `!=` comparisons. * `state` supports `=`, `!=` comparisons. * `create_time` supports `=`, `!=`,`<`, `<=`,`>`, `>=` comparisons. `create_time` must be in RFC 3339 format. * `labels` supports general map functions that is: `labels.key=value` - key:value equality `labels.key:* - key existence Some examples of using the filter are: * `state="JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED" AND display_name:"my_job_*"` * `state!="JOB_STATE_FAILED" OR display_name="my_job"` * `NOT display_name="my_job"` * `create_time>"2021-05-18T00:00:00Z"` * `labels.keyA=valueA` * `labels.keyB:*`

list.description: Lists BatchPredictionJobs in a Location.

parent.description: Required. The resource name of the Location to create the BatchPredictionJob in. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`

name.description: Required. The name of the BatchPredictionJob resource. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/batchPredictionJobs/{batch_prediction_job}`

Clients can use Operations.GetOperation or other methods to check whether the cancellation succeeded or whether the operation completed despite cancellation.
